title: ‘Most Violence Is Not Caused by Mental Illness’

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》每日电子简报DealBook的商业与政策记者。

sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克，

sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人，他们将亲临纽约市DealBook峰会的现场。

sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是一份日报。

sentences.en: Republican leaders, conservatives, and the NRA are all again pointing to mental illness in response to a series of deadly mass shootings.
sentences.zh: 共和党领袖、保守派和全国步枪协会在发生了一系列致命的大规模枪击事件后，再次将矛头指向了精神疾病。

sentences.en: But that raises a question.
sentences.zh: 但这引发了一个问题。

sentences.en: How can the mental health system stop a shooting when most shooters aren't mentally ill?
sentences.zh: 当大多数枪手并没有精神疾病时，心理健康系统如何能阻止枪击事件？

sentences.en: Today, we revisit a conversation I first had in 2018 with a psychiatrist who is wrestling with that challenge.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们重温我在2018年首次与一位正在应对这一挑战的精神病学家进行的对话。

sentences.en: Wednesday, June 8th.
sentences.zh: 6月8日，星期三。

sentences.en: That this insane monster should have ever been able to obtain a firearm.
sentences.zh: 这个疯狂的恶魔竟然能够获得枪支。

sentences.en: Ever.
sentences.zh: Ever.

sentences.en: I do not think that he should have gotten his hands on any kind of weapon.
sentences.zh: 我认为他不应该弄到任何武器。

sentences.en: That's number one.
sentences.zh: 这是第一点。

sentences.en: This individual was nuts.
sentences.zh: 这家伙脑子有毛病。

sentences.en: We don't know right now exactly why this deranged individual did this.
sentences.zh: 我们现在还不知道这个精神错乱的家伙为什么这样做。

sentences.en: Crazy madman bent on evil.
sentences.zh: 心怀恶意的疯狂狂热分子。

sentences.en: And a wacko came in and shot the five of them.
sentences.zh: 一个疯子闯进来，枪杀了他俩。

sentences.en: Who were shot by this madman.
sentences.zh: 被这个疯子枪杀的。

sentences.en: They're homicidal maniacs.
sentences.zh: 他们是凶残的狂人。

sentences.en: People like this with mental health issues.
sentences.zh: 像这样有心理健康问题的人。

sentences.en: This troubled young man fell through the cracks.
sentences.zh: 这个陷入困境的年轻人被忽视了。

sentences.en: The failure of America's mental health system.
sentences.zh: 美国心理健康系统的失败。

sentences.en: This is a mental health problem.
sentences.zh: 这是一个心理健康问题。

sentences.en: There is a mental health epidemic here which is being confused for a gun problem.
sentences.zh: 这里存在一个心理健康流行病，却被混淆成了枪支问题。

sentences.en: Again, this is a mental health issue.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这是一个心理健康问题。

sentences.en: This is not a gun issue.
sentences.zh: 这不是枪支问题。

sentences.en: The common theme with these kinds of shootings is mental illness.
sentences.zh: 这类枪击事件的共同点是精神疾病。

sentences.en: And this is something that we should not be ignoring.
sentences.zh: 这是我们不应该忽视的事情。

sentences.en: Anybody who shoots somebody else has a mental health challenge.
sentences.zh: 任何枪杀他人的人都有心理健康方面的挑战。

sentences.en: Period.
sentences.zh: Period.

sentences.en: Would you like me to, how would you like me to refer to you?
sentences.zh: 你想让我，你希望我怎么称呼你？

sentences.en: Doctor?
sentences.zh: Doctor?

sentences.en: Professionally, Dr. BarnhorSt. Personally, you can always call me Amy, but professionally,
sentences.zh: 从职业角度来说，叫巴恩霍斯特医生。私下里，你随时可以叫我艾米，但从职业角度来看，

sentences.en: Dr. BarnhorSt. Okay.
sentences.zh: 巴恩霍斯特医生。好的。

sentences.en: So Dr. Barnhorst, tell me about the day of this appointment.
sentences.zh: 那么，巴恩霍斯特医生，请告诉我这次预约当天的情景。

sentences.en: Well, it started out as just a usual day in a busy crisis unit.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它开始时只是一个繁忙的危机干预中心里寻常的一天。

sentences.en: So I work as an emergency psychiatrist in a crisis unit that's adjacent to an inpatient psychiatric hospital in California.
sentences.zh: 我在加州一家与住院精神病院相邻的危机干预中心担任急诊精神病学家。

sentences.en: We see people who are acutely ill or acutely in crisis, maybe people feeling suicidal and depressed.
sentences.zh: 我们接待病情严重或处于急性危机中的人，比如感到自杀倾向和抑郁的人。

sentences.en: Maybe some folks who were brought in because they were hearing voices.
sentences.zh: 也许还有一些因为听到幻听而被送进来的人。

sentences.en: And then the police brought this kid in.
sentences.zh: 然后警察把这个小孩带了进来。

sentences.en: He was a 21-year-old and his parents had called the cops because they had gotten concerned about some of the stuff he'd been posting on social media.
sentences.zh: 他21岁，他的父母因为担心他在社交媒体上发布的一些内容而报了警。

sentences.en: His posts had kind of gotten increasingly hostile, but were generally vague up until, you know, the last few days where he had made some specific
sentences.zh: 他的帖子变得越来越具有敌意，但总体上比较含糊，直到，你知道的，最近几天他做出了一些具体的

sentences.en: references to the Columbine shooting and something about some death and destruction.
sentences.zh: 关于科伦拜恩枪击事件的暗示，以及一些关于死亡和毁灭的内容。

sentences.en: And one of the things he referred to in his Facebook page was a day of retribution.
sentences.zh: 他在自己的Facebook主页上提到的事情之一就是复仇日。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: Hmm.

sentences.en: And when the police went to his house and spoke with the parents, the brother mentioned that
sentences.zh: 当警察去他家与父母交谈时，他的兄弟提到

sentences.en: this patient had told him he was going to try to buy a gun and the brother thought he had done so, but wasn't sure.
sentences.zh: 这个病人曾告诉他，他要尝试买一把枪，兄弟认为他已经买过了，但不确定。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: Hmm.

sentences.en: And why did the police bring him to your office?
sentences.zh: 警察为什么把他带到你的办公室？

sentences.en: They've been told about this posting on Facebook, which is alarming.
sentences.zh: 他们被告知了这些在Facebook上令人担忧的发帖。

sentences.en: Why did they bring him to you?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么把他带到你这里？

sentences.en: Well, he really hadn't committed a crime.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他其实并没有犯罪。

sentences.en: So they couldn't arrest him.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不能逮捕他。

sentences.en: But I imagine that the police were pretty worried about this guy.
sentences.zh: 但我猜警察对这家伙非常担心。

sentences.en: You know, he certainly had a lot of concerning signs and I think they brought him to
sentences.zh: 你知道，他身上确实有很多令人担忧的迹象，我想他们把他带到

sentences.en: us in the hopes that maybe the mental health system would be a way that we could prevent him from going down a bad path.
sentences.zh: 我们这里，是希望心理健康系统能够成为阻止他走上歧途的一种途径。

sentences.en: So what are you doing first?
sentences.zh: 那么你首先要做什么？

sentences.en: What's your role in this moment?
sentences.zh: 此刻你的角色是什么？

sentences.en: So my first thing is I get the chart and I flip through it and kind of see what's going on.
sentences.zh: 所以我的第一件事是拿到病历并快速翻阅，看看发生了什么。

sentences.en: For this young man, I probably would have had any records we had on him, which was none.
sentences.zh: 对于这个年轻人，我大概会有我们关于他的所有记录，那就是没有记录。

sentences.en: And the legal hold that the police brought him in on, which was just a piece of paper with a few lines, might be something as
sentences.zh: 警察带他进来时依据的法律拘留令，只是一张写着几行字的纸，上面可能写着

sentences.en: simple as making threatening postings on Facebook, comma, might have bought guns, says brother,
sentences.zh: 诸如在Facebook上发表威胁性言论，逗号，可能买过枪，兄弟说，

sentences.en: comma, parents worried.
sentences.zh: 逗号，父母很担心。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: Okay.

sentences.en: In this case, I had fairly little except that ominous information.
sentences.zh: 在这种除了那些不祥的信息外，我几乎了解不到什么。

sentences.en: So I always build a picture in my mind of what people are going to be like before I meet them.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是在见到人们之前，在脑海中构建一个关于他们会是什么样子的画面。

sentences.en: But he did not really jive with my mental image that I had built up.
sentences.zh: 但他实际上并不符合我在脑海中建立的形象。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: If I had met this young man and he seemed, for example, like in a manic episode where he was
sentences.zh: 如果我遇到这个年轻人时，他看起来，比如说，处于狂躁发作状态，

sentences.en: impulsive, where he was talking really fast, where he was delusional and grandiose, that might be
sentences.zh: 冲动，语速极快，充满妄想和夸大狂，这可能

sentences.en: indicative that he was in fact mentally ill and that maybe this idea about threatening up his school
sentences.zh: 表明他确实患有精神疾病，也许他关于袭击学校的想法

sentences.en: was secondary to a mental illness that could be treated and thereby we could prevent the shooting or the active violence.
sentences.zh: 是由可以治疗的精神疾病引起的，因此我们可以通过治疗来预防枪击或暴力行为。

sentences.en: But in the case of him, I mean, he looked not like somebody with a mental illness.
sentences.zh: 但在他身上，我的意思是，他看起来不像一个有精神疾病的人。

sentences.en: He didn't have any of those signs.
sentences.zh: 他没有任何这些迹象。

sentences.en: He was a nice enough kid, not particularly angry to me, although it was easy to see that he had some darkness in him.
sentences.zh: 他是个挺好的孩子，对我也没有特别生气，尽管很容易看出他内心有些阴暗面。

sentences.en: And I think he was a little sullen and depressed, not happy with his social standing and how things had been going at his school.
sentences.zh: 我想他当时有点阴郁和沮丧，对自己的社会地位以及在学校里的遭遇感到不满意。

sentences.en: He said that he didn't think he had a mental illness.
sentences.zh: 他说他认为自己没有精神疾病。

sentences.en: He didn't want treatment.
sentences.zh: 他不想接受治疗。

sentences.en: He didn't need treatment.
sentences.zh: 他不需要治疗。

sentences.en: He seemed more like a sad, brooding kid who was hurt and realized he had done something wrong and really wanted to go home.
sentences.zh: 他看起来更像一个悲伤、沉闷的孩子，受到了伤害，意识到自己做错了事，并且非常想回家。

sentences.en: So ultimately, you're trying to determine if this post on Facebook was coming from a place of mental illness or possibly something else.
sentences.zh: 所以归根结底，你是在试图确定Facebook上的这个帖子是源于精神疾病还是可能源于其他原因。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: Yeah.

sentences.en: So I'm trying to figure out if he is going to meet criteria to be involuntarily admitted to a psychiatric hospital.
sentences.zh: 所以我试图弄清楚他是否符合被非自愿送入精神病院的标准。

sentences.en: And in California, in order to be admitted to a psychiatric hospital involuntarily, you have to meet one of three criteria to either be dangerous to yourself,
sentences.zh: 在加州，为了被非自愿送入精神病院，你必须符合以下三个标准之一：对你自己危险、

sentences.en: dangerous to somebody else, or gravely disabled, which means that you're not able to provide for your own basic needs, like your food, clothing, and shelter.
sentences.zh: 对别人危险，或严重残疾，这意味着你无法满足自己的基本需求，比如食物、衣服和住所。

sentences.en: And you have to meet one of those three things because of a mental illness.
sentences.zh: 而且你必须是因为精神疾病才符合这三点中的一条。

sentences.en: So even if this young man is angry or showing a propensity towards violence, you'd need to
sentences.zh: 所以即使这个年轻人很愤怒或表现出暴力倾向，你也需要

sentences.en: determine that these emotions are coming from a mental illness in order to involuntarily commit him.
sentences.zh: 确定这些情绪源于精神疾病，才能将其实施非自愿收治。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: Right.

sentences.en: So at this point, I'm making a primarily clinical decision about whether or not I should admit this young man for treatment.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一点上，我主要是在做一个临床决定，决定是否应该收治这个年轻人进行治疗。

sentences.en: But I also know that my clinical decisions have legal implications for him because there's a difference between an admission to a hospital and a commitment.
sentences.zh: 但我也知道我的临床决定对他的法律有影响，因为入院治疗和强制收治是有区别的。

sentences.en: As a doctor, what I do is I make the clinical decision to admit someone to a hospital.
sentences.zh: 作为一名医生，我所做的是做出将某人收治入院的临床决定。

sentences.en: The commitment is a legal process that is done by the judge or the hearing officer.
sentences.zh: 强制收治是由法官或听证官员执行的法律程序。

sentences.en: And that's the checks and balances in the system that make sure that some doctor can't just admit people willy-nilly and hold them in a hospital indefinitely with no liberties.
sentences.zh: 这是系统中的制衡机制，确保某个医生不能随心所欲地收治人员，并将他们无限期地关在医院里剥夺自由。

sentences.en: And so if he is committed, then his name goes into a federal database of people who are prohibited from purchasing guns.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果他被强制收治，他的名字就会进入一个联邦数据库，里面记录了被禁止购买枪支的人。

sentences.en: And any time a federally licensed dealer does a background check, his name will come up as a prohibited person, and he won't be able to buy a gun.
sentences.zh: 每当联邦持牌经销商进行背景调查时，他的名字就会作为违禁人员出现，他将无法买枪。

sentences.en: But he'll still be able to purchase from private party sales and from internet sales and from gun shows, where in most states they don't do background checks.
sentences.zh: 但他仍然能够从私人聚会销售、互联网销售和枪支展销会上购买，在大多数州，这些地方不进行背景调查。

sentences.en: And so this is how someone like you interacts with what most people think of as the federal background check system that's used for gun purchases.
sentences.zh: 这就是像你这样的人如何与大多数人认为用于购枪的联邦背景调查系统进行互动。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: Yes.

sentences.en: Doctor, this feels very complicated, what you're describing, because so often people are expressing violent thoughts, but mental illness is not clear.
sentences.zh: 医生，你所描述的这感觉非常复杂，因为人们经常表达暴力想法，但精神疾病并不明显。

sentences.en: And yet, as a doctor, you want to prevent them from carrying out these acts, I assume.
sentences.zh: 然而，作为一名医生，我想你希望阻止他们实施这些行为。

sentences.en: So how do you grapple with people who fall short of that glaring mental illness, but who are expressing violent thoughts?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于那些达不到明显精神疾病标准但又在表达暴力想法的人，你该如何应对？

sentences.en: I mean, it's hard, because we do see people every day, especially in a crisis setting that we want to help, but they don't meet the criteria for involuntary help.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很难，因为我们每天都会看到一些人，尤其是在危机环境中我们想要帮助他们，但他们不符合非自愿帮助的标准。

sentences.en: And they don't want help.
sentences.zh: 而且他们不想要帮助。

sentences.en: And so we have to let them go.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须让他们离开。

sentences.en: And sometimes that involves people with the potential for violence.
sentences.zh: 有时这涉及具有暴力潜力的人。

sentences.en: And it is a balance between people's civil liberties and their right to make choices that I may not think are the best choices.
sentences.zh: 这是公民自由与他们做出我可能认为不是最佳选择的选择的权利之间的平衡。

sentences.en: It's really hard from the vantage point of being a psychiatrist to prevent violence, since most violence is not caused by mental illness.
sentences.zh: 从精神病医生的角度来看，要预防暴力真的很难，因为大多数暴力都不是由精神疾病引起的。

sentences.en: About 4% of community violence is attributable to severe mental illness.
sentences.zh: 社区暴力中约有4%可归因于严重精神疾病。

sentences.en: So that would mean that 96% of the rest of violence that occurs in a community has nothing to do with mental illness.
sentences.zh: 这就意味着，社区中发生的其余96%的暴力事件与精神疾病毫无关系。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: Correct.

sentences.en: Do you know how mental illness relates to mass shootings, specifically, in terms of cause and effect and scale?
sentences.zh: 你知道精神疾病与大规模枪击事件之间具体有怎样的因果关系和规模关联吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: Yeah.

sentences.en: I mean, so this is a tricky question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个棘手的问题。

sentences.en: We get into semantics a little bit here, because, you know, it's hard to stand by an argument that people who make posts like this, or that anybody who
sentences.zh: 我们在这里有点陷入语义学的讨论，因为，你知道的，很难支持这样一种观点，即发表这类帖子的人，或者任何

sentences.en: goes into a school and opens fire on students, is some paragon of psychological well-being.
sentences.zh: 去学校向学生开枪的人，是什么心理健康的典范。

sentences.en: I mean, I think everybody would agree that these people are not mentally well, per se.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想每个人都会同意这些人本身精神并不健康。

sentences.en: But that is really different than actually having a specific mental illness, like schizophrenia, or bipolar disorder, or major depressive disorder.
sentences.zh: 但这与真正患有特定的精神疾病（如精神分裂症、双相情感障碍或重度抑郁症）有着本质的区别。

sentences.en: A lot of the characters of these mass shooters are similar.
sentences.zh: 这些大规模枪击案凶手的很多特征都很相似。

sentences.en: And that's not to say that none of them have mental illness, because some have.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说他们当中没有人患有精神疾病，因为有些人确实有。

sentences.en: But a lot of them are just really angry, resentful, bitter young men who have similar histories of social isolation.
sentences.zh: 但他们当中很多人只是非常愤怒、怨恨、痛苦的年轻男子，有着相似的社交孤立历史。

sentences.en: They've been bullied.
sentences.zh: 他们曾遭受霸凌。

sentences.en: They've harbored revenge fantasies.
sentences.zh: 他们怀有复仇幻想。

sentences.en: They have an entitlement towards social standing, towards attention from women.
sentences.zh: 他们对社会地位、对女性的关注有一种特权感。

sentences.en: They feel like they're not getting the popularity, the attention, the recognition- That they deserve.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得自己没有得到应有的受欢迎程度、关注、认可——他们应得的。

sentences.en: That they deserve.
sentences.zh: 他们应得的。

sentences.en: So there's this idea that they're better than everybody thinks they are, and they kind of want to show the world that.
sentences.zh: 所以有一种看法认为他们比所有人想象的都要优秀，他们某种程度上想向世界证明这一点。

sentences.en: So how would the treatment of someone like that differ from the kind of treatment they would need if they were determined to be mentally ill?
sentences.zh: 那么，对这样的人的治疗，与如果他们被确定患有精神疾病时所需的治疗有何不同？

sentences.en: It seems like in either case, some kind of treatment is needed.
sentences.zh: 似乎在任何一种情况下，某种治疗都是需要的。

sentences.en: So what's the difference?
sentences.zh: 那么有什么区别呢？

sentences.en: Well, one of the big differences, you know, we do have medications for things like schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最大的区别之一是，我们确实有针对精神分裂症和双相情感障碍等疾病的药物。

sentences.en: We don't have medications for things like resentment, hatred, anger at the world.
sentences.zh: 我们没有针对怨恨、仇恨、对世界的愤怒等情绪的药物。

sentences.en: We can't fix that so well.
sentences.zh: 我们无法很好地解决这个问题。

sentences.en: So there's no way to like admit somebody like that to a psychiatric hospital, treat them over the course of the two weeks that we might be able to have them,
sentences.zh: 所以没有办法把这样的人送进精神病院，在我们可能能够留住他们的两周时间里治疗他们，

sentences.en: and then completely change the personality that they've spent their whole life building up.
sentences.zh: 然后彻底改变他们花了一生时间建立起来的个性。

sentences.en: And it sounds like this young man who's standing in front of you fits that profile more than one of a clearly mentally ill person.
sentences.zh: 听起来站在你面前的这个年轻人更符合这种特征，而不是一个患有明显精神疾病的人。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: Absolutely.

sentences.en: He fits the profile of the angry, socially isolated young man with no mental health history.
sentences.zh: 他符合那个愤怒、社交孤立、没有心理健康病史的年轻男子的特征。

sentences.en: So what's going through your head as you make this decision whether or not to admit him?
sentences.zh: 所以在你决定是否收治他时，你脑子里在想些什么？

sentences.en: So in my mind, I'm thinking to myself, this young man does not appear to be mentally ill to me.
sentences.zh: 所以在我心里，我在想，在我看来，这个年轻人并不像是精神病患者。

sentences.en: He does appear to potentially be dangerous, but that's not something that is going to be changed by admitting him to a psychiatric hospital.
sentences.zh: 他的确可能具有危险性，但这并不是通过将他送入精神病院就能改变的。

sentences.en: And if I send him home, then I'm concerned that I, you know, had my chance to intervene with the next mass shooter and I did nothing.
sentences.zh: 如果我把他放回家，我就会担心，你知道的，我本有机会阻止下一个大规模枪击案的凶手，却什么也没做。

sentences.en: And now he's back home with his gun.
sentences.zh: 而现在他带着枪回到了家里。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took
sentences.zh: 即使在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会里当DJ时，每晚你也会带上

sentences.en: 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 300件你最珍贵的私人物品去工作。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把一个DJ台变成了一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，里面摆满了漂亮的、有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》App？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 免费畅读？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》App时，你在App内的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》App，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Dr. Barnhorst, you've spoken to this young man.
sentences.zh: 那么，巴恩霍斯特医生，你和这位年轻人谈过。

sentences.en: You've learned that he has posted on Facebook something quite scary.
sentences.zh: 你了解到他在Facebook上发布了一些相当吓人的内容。

sentences.en: You've learned that he may have just purchased a gun you don't know.
sentences.zh: 你了解到他可能刚刚买了一把枪，而你并不知情。

sentences.en: And now it's your job to decide whether or not to commit him for a serious mental illness.
sentences.zh: 现在你的工作是决定是否以患有严重精神疾病为由对其实施强制收治。

sentences.en: What do you decide to do?
sentences.zh: 你决定怎么做？

sentences.en: He did not look to me like he had a mental illness.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，他看起来不像有精神病。

sentences.en: He did not look to me like he technically met the standards for involuntary commitment.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，从技术上讲，他并不符合非自愿收治的标准。

sentences.en: But I really didn't want to be wrong.
sentences.zh: 但我真的不想弄错。

sentences.en: And in the end, I decided to admit him because there's some leeway in the statute.
sentences.zh: 最后，我决定接纳他住院，因为法规中有一些回旋余地。

sentences.en: So it's ultimately up to the judge to make the decision of whether or not he gets committed officially.
sentences.zh: 所以最终还是要由法官来决定他是否被正式收治。

sentences.en: So I admitted him.
sentences.zh: 所以我让他住院了。

sentences.en: So you erred on the side of caution to get him into this kind of mental health legal pipeline.
sentences.zh: 所以你采取了谨慎的态度，把他送进了这种精神健康法律流程中。

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It sounds, Dr., like you're saying, part of you understood quite clearly that he might not be mentally ill.
sentences.zh: 医生，听起来你的意思是，你的一部分内心很清楚他可能并没有精神病。

sentences.en: But you were making a kind of civic as well as medical decision to keep him out of the general population.
sentences.zh: 但你做出了一种既是公民层面也是医疗层面的决定，目的是把他隔离在普通人群之外。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the principles of practicing medicine is that the higher the risk of the possibility, the more certain you want to be that it's not the case.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，行医的原则之一是，可能性带来的风险越高，你就越需要确信事实并非如此。

sentences.en: So if I'm worried that somebody might or might not go home and punch a wall, I'm willing to be fairly liberal in making a mistake
sentences.zh: 所以如果我担心某个人可能会或可能不会回家去捶墙，我愿意在犯错时

sentences.en: there, much more so liberal than if I'm worried somebody might or might not go home and shoot up a school.
sentences.zh: 表现得相当宽松，这比我担心某个人可能会或可能不会回家去学校枪击要宽松得多。

sentences.en: You can live with one, not the other.
sentences.zh: 你可以接受其中一种情况，而不能接受另一种。

sentences.en: I am willing to let them a little bit of freedom.
sentences.zh: 我愿意给他们一点自由。

sentences.en: If the risk of my giving them some freedom and letting them go is that they might shoot a bunch of people into school, I need to be really, really
sentences.zh: 如果我给他们一些自由并放他们走的风险是他们可能会在学校枪杀一群人，我需要非常、非常

sentences.en: confident that I'm right and that that is not going to happen.
sentences.zh: 自信我是对的，而且那种事不会发生。

sentences.en: And what happened?
sentences.zh: 后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: I admitted him to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 我让他住进了医院。

sentences.en: He went before the hearing officer a few days later and the hearing officer determined that he was not dangerous because of a mental illness.
sentences.zh: 几天后他出席了听证官的听证会，听证官判定他并没有因为精神疾病而具有危险性。

sentences.en: And then he's no longer involuntarily held, so he's free to go.
sentences.zh: 然后他不再被非自愿扣留，所以他可以自由离开了。

sentences.en: So you had to let him go.
sentences.zh: 所以你不得不放他走。

sentences.en: The system had to let him go.
sentences.zh: 体制不得不放他走。

sentences.en: Yeah, we had to let him go.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们不得不放他走。

sentences.en: So, doctor, does this man end up on the federal background check system, given the way this is played out?
sentences.zh: 那么，医生，鉴于事情的发展，这个人最终会进入联邦背景调查系统吗？

sentences.en: No, because the judge did not certify his commitment in court, he does not land on the federal background check system's list of prohibited persons.
sentences.zh: 不会，因为法官没有在法庭上签发他的收治令，他不会进入联邦背景调查系统的禁止持枪人员名单。

sentences.en: But because I admitted him to the hospital, he does meet criteria for a five-year prohibition just within California.
sentences.zh: 但由于我让他住了院，他确实符合仅在加利福尼亚州实行五年禁令的标准。

sentences.en: That prohibition will expire in a couple years.
sentences.zh: 这个禁令将在几年后到期。

sentences.en: And were he to move to another state, he would still be able to buy a firearm there in the meantime?
sentences.zh: 如果他搬到另一个州，在此期间他仍然可以在那里买枪吗？

sentences.en: Do you think that this system failed this young man in this moment and, as a result, failed the rest of us?
sentences.zh: 你认为这个体制在这一刻辜负了这个年轻人，并因此辜负了我们其他人吗？

sentences.en: You know, it's hard for me to say that this system failed this young man because this young man is not who the system was set up to help.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我很难说这个体制辜负了这个年轻人，因为这个年轻人并不是这个体制建立来帮助的对象。

sentences.en: He's not somebody that we have a treatment or a cure for
sentences.zh: 他不是那种我们有治疗或治愈方法的人

sentences.en: because he wasn't mentally ill.
sentences.zh: 因为他没有精神病。

sentences.en: The unfortunate part is the criminal system couldn't help him either because he hadn't done anything criminal.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，刑事体制也帮不了他，因为他没有做出任何犯罪行为。

sentences.en: So what do you think when you hear gun rights advocates talking now so much about mental health?
sentences.zh: 那么，当你听到枪支权利倡导者现在如此多地谈论心理健康时，你有什么想法？

sentences.en: Do you think there's an understanding of what that actually means in practice?
sentences.zh: 你认为他们理解这在实践中究竟意味着什么吗？

sentences.en: I think there's not.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们没有。

sentences.en: And I think it's important for folks to have a better sense of what it looks like played out in practice, which is it doesn't look very good.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们最好对它在实践中的实际情况有一个更好的了解，那就是，情况看起来并不太好。

sentences.en: There's not a lot that in actuality we can do for these people.
sentences.zh: 实际上我们能为这些人做的事情并不多。

sentences.en: And the irony is I think a lot of the folks who point towards the mental health system as being a less restrictive way of decreasing gun violence because they don't
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，我认为许多将心理健康系统视为减少枪支暴力的非限制性途径的人，因为他们不

sentences.en: want to lose their rights to own firearMs. The part of that they're missing because they don't see
sentences.zh: 想失去拥有枪支的权利。他们没有看到

sentences.en: what happens in the real mental health world is that if we were going to really try to prevent
sentences.zh: 现实精神健康世界里发生的事情，那就是，如果我们真的要在精神健康系统内部尝试预防

sentences.en: violence and mass shootings within the mental health system, we would have to expand the net
sentences.zh: 暴力和大规模枪击事件，我们就必须极大地扩大

sentences.en: of who we were allowed to involuntarily detain and hold enormously in order to find those one or two people in thousands that might actually perpetrate mass violence.
sentences.zh: 我们被允许非自愿拘留和扣留的人员网络，以便在成千上万的人中找到那一个或两个可能真正实施大规模暴力的人。

sentences.en: Would we have to therefore expand the definition of mental illness?
sentences.zh: 因此，我们是否必须扩大精神疾病的定义？

sentences.en: I mean, it's hard to expand the definition of an illness, but I think we would be talking about dramatically expanding the reaches of the mental health system
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很难扩大一种疾病的定义，但我认为我们讨论的是大幅扩大精神健康系统的范围

sentences.en: and largely the involuntary mental health system because mostly we're looking for people who are not seeking treatment on their own.
sentences.zh: 主要是非自愿精神健康系统的范围，因为我们主要寻找的是那些没有主动寻求治疗的人。

sentences.en: So what that looks like is that we would lower the bar really far in terms of who we would be able to involuntarily commit.
sentences.zh: 所以这看起来就像是，我们在能够非自愿收治哪些人这方面把标准降得极低。

sentences.en: And it would be almost every angry young man who had a history of social isolation, being bullied, who had an interest in
sentences.zh: 几乎每一个有社交孤立史、被欺凌史、对

sentences.en: violent video games and collecting guns, whoever made macabre sounding Facebook posts, or comments about wishing everybody at his school were dead.
sentences.zh: 暴力视频游戏和收集枪支感兴趣、曾在Facebook上发表过毛骨悚然的言论或评论说希望学校里的每个人都死掉的愤怒年轻人，都会被波及。

sentences.en: That's actually a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是很多人。

sentences.en: And it's easy in hindsight to look at mass shooters and say they showed all the warning signs.
sentences.zh: 事后诸葛亮很容易去看待大规模枪击案凶手，并说他们表现出了所有的警告信号。

sentences.en: But when you look forward, that's a lot of people that you would have to take out of their world and out of their lives
sentences.zh: 但当你向前看时，会有那么多人需要被带出他们的世界和生活

sentences.en: and involuntarily detained in the mental health system and probably to not much end.
sentences.zh: 并在精神健康系统中被非自愿拘留，而且很可能没有什么结果。

sentences.en: What do you mean to not much end?
sentences.zh: 你说的没有什么结果是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, eventually we have to let them go.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最终我们不得不放他们走。

sentences.en: It's unlikely that we'd be able to fix them.
sentences.zh: 我们不太可能修复他们。

sentences.en: So even if we were allowed to keep them for three weeks or three months,
sentences.zh: 所以即使我们被允许把他们留三周或三个月，

sentences.en: I don't know that we would be really solving the problem.
sentences.zh: 我也不知道我们是否真的能解决问题。

sentences.en: We would just be keeping them out of circulation for a little while.
sentences.zh: 我们只是把他们隔离了一小段时间。

sentences.en: Doctor, I wonder how often you think about this young man who you admitted and then who the court system let go and who now roams the world.
sentences.zh: 医生，我想知道你多久会想起这个被你收治、然后被法院系统释放、如今在外面四处游荡的年轻人一次。

sentences.en: I think about him every time there's a school shooting.
sentences.zh: 每次发生校园枪击案时我都会想起他。

sentences.en: Doctor, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 医生，非常感谢您。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, lawmakers offered new details about what could become the first major news set of federal gun restrictions in decades.
sentences.zh: 周二，议员们提供了关于可能成为几十年来第一套重大的联邦枪支限制措施的新细节。

sentences.en: One of the proposals under discussion is the creation of a system that would screen gun buyers under the age of 21 for juvenile offenses and previous episodes
sentences.zh: 正在讨论的提案之一是建立一个系统，对21岁以下的购枪者进行有关少年犯罪和以往

sentences.en: involving mental health.
sentences.zh: 心理健康事件的筛查。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: In a closely watched election on Tuesday night, residents of San Francisco voted to remove the
sentences.zh: 在周二晚上一场备受瞩目的选举中，旧金山居民投票罢免了

sentences.en: city's Democratic district attorney, Chessa Boudin, who faced criticism that his liberal policies have led to an increase in crime.
sentences.zh: 该市的民主党地区检察官切沙·布丁，他曾面临批评，称其自由派政策导致了犯罪率上升。

sentences.en: There is little evidence that Boudin's policies have contributed to
sentences.zh: 几乎没有证据表明布丁的政策导致了

sentences.en: San Francisco's rising crime rate.
sentences.zh: 旧金山不断上升的犯罪率。

sentences.en: But his message of leniency for criminals has nevertheless upset voters and served as a warning to Democrats that voters are worried about crime.
sentences.zh: 但他对罪犯宽大处理的信息依然惹恼了选民，并向民主党人发出了一个警告，即选民对犯罪感到担忧。

sentences.en: And a panel advising the FDA has recommended that the agency authorize the use of a fourth vaccine against COVID-19 made by the biotechnology firm Novavax.
sentences.zh: 一个向FDA提供咨询的小组建议该机构授权使用由生物技术公司诺瓦瓦克斯（Novavax）制造的第四种针对新冠肺炎的疫苗。

sentences.en: Unlike the COVID vaccines from Pfizer and Moderna, which rely on messenger RNA, the Novavax vaccine employs traditional vaccine technology used in vaccines against the flu.
sentences.zh: 与依赖信使RNA的辉瑞和莫德纳新冠疫苗不同，诺瓦瓦克斯疫苗采用的是流感疫苗中使用的传统疫苗技术。

sentences.en: That, experts said, might encourage vaccine skeptics to try the Novavax vaccine.
sentences.zh: 专家表示，这可能会鼓励疫苗怀疑论者尝试诺瓦瓦克斯疫苗。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由安妮·布朗、克莱尔·特内斯凯特、蕾切尔·奎斯特、林赛·加里森、

sentences.zh: 迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊、西奥·巴尔科姆、里基·诺韦茨基和穆吉·扎迪制作。

sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由吉姆·布伦伯格和

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称为改革派的人。
